questions.problem: Which number line shows the values of $x$ that satisfy $2x-7<5$ and $3x+3\ge -3?$
questions.worked_solution:
To solve compound "and" inequalities, we solve each inequality separately and then find their intersection. 

- First, we solve $2x-7<5\,:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}2x-7 & <5 \\ 2x-7+7 & <5+7 \\ 2x & <12 \\ \frac{2x}{2} & <\frac{12}{2} \\ x & <6\end{aligned}
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14194110/assets/c3f9a8f8d42c4e029fd7d5ce26ef05d9834f6bf443aa61c1e3a89d228e79efc5.png)

$$

$$

- Then, we solve $3x+3\ge -3\,:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}3x+3 & \ge -3 \\ 3x+3-3 & \ge -3-3 \\ 3x & \ge -6 \\ \frac{3x}{3} & \ge \frac{-6}{3} \\ x & \ge -2\end{aligned}
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14194110/assets/6281ea0ab80bf4a785d92026a5ccd0929659851e177e8cc7d6f41a7994a29791.png)

$$

$$

To find the values of $x$ that satisfy both inequalities, we find where the two solutions overlap:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14194110/assets/1da1439e3fff4e39a6b891d8b295eada7e67b49763bca0b080a076c833242d7e.png)

Thus, the final solution is $-2\le x<6.$

\begin{aligned}2-7x & \ge 2 \\ 2-7x-2 & \ge 2-2 \\ -7x & \ge 0 \\ (-1)\cdot (-7x) & \le (-1)\cdot 0 \\ 7x & \le 0 \\ \frac{7x}{7} & \le \frac{0}{7} \\ x & \le 0\end{aligned}

$$
\begin{aligned}10x-3 & \ge 7 \\ 10x-3+3 & \ge 7+3 \\ 10x & \ge 10 \\ \frac{10x}{10} & \ge \frac{10}{10} \\ x & \ge 1\end{aligned}
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14194110/assets/9d2d2e7b05bd4bcaf964353266e35bb12f406372ade7255accf6dc3503046f5c.png)

canonical_examples.problem: Find the set of values of $x$ that satisfy $1 \lt 3x-2 \leq 7$ and $2-3x \leq -4.$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
To solve compound "and" inequalities, we solve each inequality separately and then find their intersection.

- First, we solve $1 \lt 3x-2 \leq 7 \,\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}1 & <3x-2\le 7 \\ 1+2 & <3x-2+2\le 7+2 \\ 3 & <3x\le 9 \\ \frac{3}{3} & <\frac{3x}{3}\le \frac{9}{3} \\ 1 & <x\le 3\end{aligned}
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14194110/assets/341633f5e132e1ab07af8969161c20443d65aec7e89ce0bc600868504dd19f9b.png)

- Then, we solve  $2-3x \leq -4 \,\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}2-3x & \le -4 \\ 2-3x-2 & \le -4-2 \\ -3x & \le -6 \\ (-1)\cdot (-3x) & \ge (-1)\cdot (-6) \\ 3x & \ge 6 \\ \frac{3x}{3} & \ge \frac{6}{3} \\ x & \ge 2\end{aligned}
$$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14194110/assets/06dafae801f6ed3900474c72437eb5a40376ed06bebf3c6eb568e6237c2d930d.png)

To find the values of $x$ that satisfy both inequalities, we find where the two solutions overlap:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14194110/assets/9b3bd118d0940d6336a32c25b8556dccb3c4085f75da7d3d8628725cf9105071.png)

   

Thus, the final solution is $x \in [2,3].$

$$
\begin{aligned}3x+9 & \ge 0 \\ 3x+9-9 & \ge 0-9 \\ 3x & \ge -9 \\ \frac{3x}{3} & \ge \frac{-9}{3} \\ x & \ge -3\end{aligned}

- Then, we solve $2x \leq -2\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}2x & \le -2 \\ \frac{2x}{2} & \le \frac{-2}{2} \\ x & \le -1\end{aligned}
$$

The solution to this inequality is shown on the number line below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14194110/assets/35e30bc9c45b08793d847c8750698f7d9dab781438405239ed4483ce82f2dcfb.png)

To find the values of $x$ that satisfy both inequalities, we find where the two solutions overlap:

Thus, the final solution is $\color{blue}-3 \leq x \leq -1.$
